target.title: feat: chat welcome shows an animated Clawd hero and recent chats instead of canned suggestions
target.body:
Closes #104245

## What Problem This Solves

The new-session welcome screen underused its space and aged poorly for real users. The default Clawd avatar was a small static PNG boxed inside a bordered tile, the "Ready to chat" pill added noise without carrying information, and the four canned suggestion chips kept showing forever — even for users who already have plenty of their own chats, for whom jumping back into recent work is far more useful than sample prompts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The welcome hero now reuses the existing animated lobster sprite (the sidebar lobster-pet renderer) instead of the static PNG: bigger, borderless, with a gentle idle loop (breathe, blink, an occasional claw wave) that respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. The status badge is gone. When the user has user-created sessions (dashboard chats, worktree sessions — not channel-bound Discord/Telegram/… sessions), the welcome lists the five most recent as clickable rows that switch to that session; the canned suggestions remain only for users with no such sessions. Recents reuse the sidebar's visible-row rules and the canonical selected-agent resolution (including bare `global` session keys, where the agent lives in host state rather than the key).

## User Impact

Every Control UI user sees a livelier, less boxed-in welcome on new/empty sessions. Users with existing chats get one-click resumption of recent work instead of static sample prompts; new users keep the suggestion chips. Custom assistant avatars (image or text) still render, just larger.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts` — 155 tests pass, including new coverage: recents replace suggestions and open on click, channel-bound-only sessions keep suggestions, bare-global keys scope recents to the selected agent, and the Clawd fallback renders without the badge.
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean after `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` (removed `chat.welcome.ready`, added `chat.welcome.recentSessions`).
- `pnpm check:changed` green.
- Screenshots (mock-gateway harness, `ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.ts`): posted in the PR comment below — one with no user sessions (suggestions) and one with mixed sessions (recents shown, Discord group excluded, worktree subtitle rendered).

target.title: feat(macos): onboarding mascot reacts with moods, randomized idle behavior, and Easter eggs
target.body:
Closes #104253 ## What Problem This Solves The onboarding hero mascot plays one fixed loop regardless of what setup is doing: it floats, wiggles, and blinks identically whether the Gateway install just failed or the AI connection test just succeeded. The character that fronts the entire first-run experience never reacts to it, and there is nothing playful to discover. ## Why This Change Was Made The shared mascot view now has a small behavior engine (`OpenClawMascotAnimator`) that owns per-mood animation loops, entrance gestures, randomized micro-behavior, and interaction Easter eggs, while the drawing stays in the existing `Canvas` vector (new pose channels: gaze, eyelids, happy-arc eyes, mouth, blush, body tilt/squash, antenna droop, dizzy eyes, sparkle/heart/zzz particles). The macOS onboarding maps flow state to a mood (`OnboardingView.mascotMood`); the mascot component owns how each mood looks and moves. The base idle loop keeps the exact openclaw.ai hero timings (4s float, 2s antenna wiggle) so the brand mark still reads the same at rest. Public API is additive — existing `OpenClawMascotView(floats:)` call sites are unchanged, and `interactive:` defaults to off so the mascot never swallows taps meant for enclosing controls (e.g. the About window's GitHub button). ## User Impact During onboarding the little guy now lives the setup with you: - **Moods track the flow**: curious on the connection-choice page, thinking (eyes scanning up, antennae twitching) while the Gateway installs or an AI candidate is live-tested, sad (drooped antennae, dim eyes, frown, occasional sigh) when an install or every AI candidate fails, and celebrating (jump, raised claws, sparkles, big grin) the moment "Your AI is ready" lands and on the final page. Attentive-and-compact on the chat page; happy once all permissions are granted. - **Randomized idle life**: blink cadence with occasional double blinks, random glances, claw snaps, and rare quirks — a wink, a lean-out-of-frame peek, an antenna glow zap, a tiny hop, and (rarely) a sneeze. Seeded RNG makes every run unique but deterministic in tests. - **Easter eggs**: eyes follow your pointer; a click earns a hop, wave, or wink; three quick clicks earn blushing hearts; six make it dizzy (orbiting spiral eyes, wobble, recovery head-shake). Leave it alone for a minute and it falls asleep (drifting z's, yawns) — it nods off twice as fast between 23:00 and 05:00 — and a click startles it awake. It also waves hello shortly after the window opens. - **Reduce Motion** users get static per-mood expressions instead of animation. The macOS About window mascot and the iOS hero marks (Settings About mark, onboarding wizard glyphs, gateway quick-setup glyph) are opted into the same click Easter eggs; About's GitHub navigation moves to the existing link row below the mascot. Marks that sit inside controls (sidebar gateway header, compact header marks) stay passive. ## Evidence All renders below are produced by the production drawing/behavior code (`OpenClawMascotCanvas` + seeded `OpenClawMascotAnimator`), captured via `ImageRenderer`. ### Emotion overview ![mascot emotions contact sheet](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/mascot-emotions-contact-sheet.png) ### Behavior clips | | | | --- | --- | | **Idle + hello wave** (welcome page)
![idle](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/mascot-idle-hello.gif) | **Celebrating** ("Your AI is ready", finish page)
![celebrating](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/mascot-celebrating.gif) | | **Thinking** (install / AI live-test)
![thinking](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/mascot-thinking.gif) | **Sad** (install/AI failure)
![sad](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/mascot-sad.gif) | | **Hearts** (3 quick clicks)
![hearts](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/mascot-hearts.gif) | **Dizzy** (6+ rapid clicks, then recovery shake)
![dizzy](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/mascot-dizzy.gif) | | **Sleepy** (idle ~1min; click to wake)
![sleepy](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/mascot-sleepy.gif) | **Sneeze** (rare idle quirk)
![sneeze](https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/mascot-sneeze.gif) | Artifact manifest (SHA256 per file): https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/pr-macos-mascot-emotions-20260711/artifact-manifest.json ### Tests and gates - `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: `swift test --filter OpenClawMascotAnimatorTests` — 13 tests: pose channels stay inside the drawable 120x120 art box for every mood across 30s timelines, blink cadence bounds, celebration entrance, sad droop signature, hearts/dizzy tap escalation, sleep/wake lifecycle, no-sleep for non-interactive views (they have no wake path), pointer gaze tracking, seeded determinism, Reduce Motion static poses, channel clamping. - `apps/macos`: `swift test --filter OnboardingMascotMoodTests` — 7 tests table-driving the flow-state → mood mapping (probe states, install lifecycle, AI phases, permissions, chat, ready). - `swift build` clean for `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` (macOS and iOS-simulator cross-compile) and `apps/macos`; `scripts/format-swift.sh` and `swiftlint` clean. - Autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh): one accepted finding — auto-sleep originally applied to non-interactive mascots that can never be tapped awake — fixed by gating auto-sleep on `interactive:`; final rerun clean.

target.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup
target.body:
Fixes #75658

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` did not preview stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files, and the apply summary did not report when those physical archive files were removed. Operators could see only unreferenced-artifact counts even when deleted/reset session archives were the files consuming disk.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup command already had an archive retention helper, but dry-run did not call it and store maintenance discarded its removal count. This change reuses the existing archive-retention rules for both preview and apply reporting instead of adding a second cleanup policy.

Reviewer follow-up: dry-run cleanup now mirrors apply ordering. Deleted/reset archive cleanup is previewed before disk-budget enforcement, and the disk-budget sweep excludes paths already attributed to archive cleanup. This keeps dry-run `archiveCleanup` and `diskBudget` attribution aligned with apply output.

## User Impact

Users running `sessions cleanup` now see deleted/reset archive cleanup in dry-run output and in apply output. Forced cleanup also scans the store directory for stale deleted archives even when no session rows were removed, while `resetArchiveRetention: false` still preserves reset archives.

## Evidence

Focused validation:

- `CI=true pnpm run lint:tmp:session-accessor-boundary`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/sessions-cleanup.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-files.fs.archive-cleanup.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/config/sessions/cleanup-service.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.ts src/config/sessions/disk-budget.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-files.fs.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json src/config/sessions/cleanup-service.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.ts src/config/sessions/disk-budget.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-files.fs.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Real CLI proof, with temp paths redacted:

```text
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts --no-color sessions cleanup --store "$TMP/archive-store/sessions.json" --dry-run --enforce
Session store: $TMP/archive-store/sessions.json
Maintenance mode: enforce
Entries: 0 -> 0 (remove 0)
Would prune missing transcripts: 0
Would retire stale direct DM sessions: 0
Would prune stale model-run probes: 0
Would prune stale: 0
Would cap overflow: 0
Would prune deleted/reset archives: 2
Would prune unreferenced artifacts: 0

after dry-run files:
["fresh.jsonl.deleted.2026-06-26T00-00-00.000Z","redacted-deleted.jsonl.deleted.2026-01-01T00-00-00.000Z","redacted-reset.jsonl.reset.2026-01-01T00-00-00.000Z","sessions.json"]

$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts --no-color sessions cleanup --store "$TMP/archive-store/sessions.json" --enforce
Session store: $TMP/archive-store/sessions.json
Applied maintenance. Current entries: 0
Pruned deleted/reset archives: 2

after apply files:
["fresh.jsonl.deleted.2026-06-26T00-00-00.000Z","sessions.json"]
```

Current-head disk-budget attribution proof from the real CLI in JSON mode, with `maxDiskBytes: 1000`, `highWaterBytes: 900`, and one oversized stale deleted archive:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$TMP/openclaw.json" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$TMP/state" node --import tsx src/entry.ts --no-color sessions cleanup --store "$TMP/archive-store/sessions.json" --dry-run --enforce --json
```

```json
{
  "agentId": "main",
  "storePath": "$TMP/archive-store/sessions.json",
  "mode": "enforce",
  "dryRun": true,
  "beforeCount": 1,
  "afterCount": 1,
  "missing": 0,
  "dmScopeRetired": 0,
  "modelRunPruned": 0,
  "pruned": 0,
  "capped": 0,
  "archiveCleanup": {
    "scannedFiles": 1,
    "removedFiles": 1
  },
  "unreferencedArtifacts": {
    "scannedFiles": 2,
    "removedFiles": 0,
    "freedBytes": 0,
    "olderThanMs": 604800000
  },
  "diskBudget": {
    "totalBytesBefore": 85,
    "totalBytesAfter": 85,
    "removedFiles": 0,
    "removedEntries": 0,
    "freedBytes": 0,
    "maxBytes": 1000,
    "highWaterBytes": 900,
    "overBudget": false
  },
  "wouldMutate": true
}
```

This shows the oversized stale archive is attributed to `archiveCleanup` first, and the disk-budget sweep no longer claims the same file.

Not run:

- `codex review --base origin/main` was attempted, but the local approval policy rejected the command because it would export the unpublished diff/repository context to an external service.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted: yes. I used Codex to inspect the issue, avoid duplicate PRs, implement the patch, and run the focused validation above.
